title: Watchlog field notes — Apr 11 2028
content:
Summary:
- Window: 0200-1000 UTC, Apr 11 2028 (night -> midshift handover). Primary focus: slow tail latency observed on hosted API model v2-falcon-quant; sporadic 95/99 spikes between 03:10–03:40 UTC. No full outage, elevated error rate briefly for short-running contexts.

What I saw (timeline):
- 03:06 UTC — Pager: automated latency alert (threshold: 95th > 450ms sustained 3m). Burst of ~12m elevated 95th.
- 03:09 UTC — Initial triage: pod CPU pegged on a subset of inference workers in cluster eu-west-2a. Per-host load indicated long GC-like pauses (smoothed CPU % spiking then dropping).
- 03:12 UTC — Route-of-last-resort: traffic redistributed to other availability zone; latency degraded but request success rate improved.
- 03:20 UTC — Rollback: Canary model variant v2-falcon-quant-2 (recent quant build) was pulled from rotation for eu-west region per routing policy (ticket INF-2148 created).
- 03:32 UTC — Observed residual tail spikes traced to a KV-cache hot-key pattern (same customer prefix surged), causing cache thrashing and backend cold-starts for some GPU workers.
- 03:45 UTC — Closed pager at 03:50 UTC after mitigation and monitoring confirmed 95/99 returned to baseline.

Actions taken (what we did):
- Immediate: increased autoscale buffer for Dedicated pool in eu-west to +2 workers to absorb load spikes (manual override).
- Routing: temporarily set routing policy to prefer region fallback (eu-west -> eu-north) for non-enterprise plans for 30 minutes.
- Model routing: removed the recently onboarded quant build from rotation (v2-falcon-quant-2) — rollback flag set in routing control plane.
- Cache: evicted top 50 hot keys (identified by prefix) from distributed KV-cache and disabled cache-population for that prefix for 15m to allow warm re-fill under controlled rate.
- Observability: enabled increased span sampling for model inference traces and turned on debug-level kv-cache metrics for the eu-west cluster for 2 hours.

Current state at handover:
- Systems: healthy. 95/99 latencies back near baseline (95th ~220ms). Error rate normal.
- Residual notes: cache hit ratio for that prefix still low (~18%) after eviction; traffic for the offending keyset has dropped but not returned to baseline.
- Open ticket: INF-2148 documenting the incident, mitigation steps, and follow-ups.

Follow-ups / action items (owners):
- DIEGO: automate hot-key detection -> create alert for "kv-hot-key > X writes/min". Jira: INF-2152. ETA: EOD Apr 13.
- JIN: expand cache eviction tool to allow prefix pattern dry-run (safer ops). PR referenced: infra#479 (see linked artifacts). ETA: Apr 18.
- AISHA (me): draft postmortem skeleton and initial timeline (start here, fill gaps with logs): link to INF-2148. ETA: Apr 12 morning.
- ENG-SERVING: assess quant build perf regressions vs baseline (compare kernel selection logs for v2-falcon-quant-2). Owner: eng-serving-runtime team. Requested by Apr 15.
- PRODUCT: evaluate whether rate-limits or fair-queueing rules should be applied to API keys that cause hot prefixes. Product lead: S. Moreno. Meeting requested.

Quick runbook / how to reproduce the triage steps (for next oncall):
1) Check alerts: Grafana watch - panel "api/latency/95th - region" -> filter eu-west.
2) Identify affected hosts: run `kubectl top pods -n inference --sort-by=cpu` or use cluster-host-level heatmap.
3) Check recent deploys: look at routing-control history `routingctl history --region eu-west --last 2h` (quick check for model variant swaps).
4) Inspect KV cache: `kvctl top-prefixes --region eu-west --window 15m` -> if top prefix > 10% of operations, consider eviction and temp-population-disable.
5) If autoscale doesn't respond: use infra-admin to scale pool: `infractl pool scale --pool dedicated-eu-west --delta +2` then monitor.
6) If quant build suspected: remove variant with `routingctl withdraw --model v2-falcon-quant-2 --region eu-west` -> observe.

Notes to next shift / unresolved questions:
- Why did the quant build correlate with high CPU/GPU context switch behavior? Need kernel-level trace; eng-serving to check scheduler and fused-kernel selection logs.
- Customer pattern: the offending prefix appears to be a single high-volume integration test (non-prod key?). Product to confirm whether API key belongs to testing customer and consider throttle.
- Are autoscaler sensitivity thresholds tuned for short GC-like spikes? Might need smoothing window bump.

Short checklist for handoff (do these before closing out):
- [ ] Confirm INF-2148 timeline has full logs attached (Aisha)
- [ ] Confirm INF-2152 alert created and initial triage notes added (Diego)
- [ ] Mark kv-cache prefix rule disabled flag with expiration (Jin)
- [ ] Keep debug-level kv metrics ON until 12:00 UTC Apr 11, unless noise is too high (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Leave a pointer in the daily SRE digest thread (Slack #sre-ops) summarizing mitigation and next steps (Aisha)

Context / miscellaneous (short):
- This was a noisy-oncall with multiple small contributors: hot-key traffic + recent quant variant + autoscale lag. None alone would have caused persistent degradation but together they pushed to threshold.
- No customer SLA breaches observed; emailed CS to flag possible customer impact per policy (CS ticket CS-879).
- Investigation notes attached: saved flamegraphs + trace snippets in the INF-2148 Confluence page.

Last-minute ops notes (for whoever picks up next):
- If you see a repeat within 30m: call eng-serving-runtime and ask them to temporarily block the quant build globally (not just region) until patch.
- If the cache hit ratio for that prefix is still <25% after 2h, escalate to infra-core for possible eviction strategy redesign.

Questions I couldn't answer during shift:
- Exact root cause of GC-like CPU behavior on those hosts (app-level GC vs host-level kernel scheduler).
- Whether the customer key causing hot prefix is due to a test harness or a production ETL job.

End notes:
- Leaving logs snapshot locations in INF-2148.
- Ping me in #sre-ops if anything regresses tonight; I'll be reachable until 12:30 UTC.

-- Aisha
(onsite SRE, night -> midshift)
